questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which international organisation is Nigeria a founding member of, established in 1945?
questions.explanation: Nigeria joined the United Nations in 1960 upon independence, though the UN itself was founded in 1945.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a major indigenous language widely spoken in and around Kwara State, alongside English and Yoruba?
questions.explanation: Nupe is a significant indigenous language spoken by communities in and around Kwara State and neighbouring Niger State, alongside the more widely spoken Yoruba.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which is the largest ocean in the world?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of the world's oceans.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period?
questions.explanation: GDP specifically measures the value of goods and services produced within a country's borders, regardless of the nationality of the producers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these is a common cause of erosion in parts of southeastern Nigeria?
options: Gully formation from rainfall and poor land use
questions.explanation: Gully erosion, worsened by heavy rainfall and poor land management, is a major issue in southeastern Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which regional body promotes economic integration among West African countries?
questions.explanation: ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States) promotes economic integration in West Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In what year did Nigeria become a republic?
questions.explanation: Nigeria became a republic on October 1, 1963, with Nnamdi Azikiwe as the first President.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: How many senators represent each state in Nigeria's National Assembly?
questions.explanation: Each of Nigeria's 36 states is represented by 3 senators.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In which year did Nigeria win the FIFA U-17 World Cup for the first time?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's Golden Eaglets won the first FIFA U-17 World Cup in China in 1985.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who is generally credited with leading the Sokoto Jihad in the early 19th century, later founding the Sokoto Caliphate?
questions.explanation: Uthman Dan Fodio led the Sokoto Jihad in the early 19th century, a religious and political reform movement that resulted in the founding of the Sokoto Caliphate.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What does GDP stand for in economics?
questions.explanation: GDP measures the total value of goods and services produced within a country.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which planet is the closest to the Sun in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet and the one closest to the Sun in our solar system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian author wrote 'Half of a Yellow Sun'?
questions.explanation: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie wrote 'Half of a Yellow Sun', set during the Biafran War.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a major cash crop historically associated with the Middle Belt region of Nigeria, including areas around Kwara State?
questions.explanation: The Middle Belt region, including Kwara State, has historically been associated with the cultivation of crops such as guinea corn (sorghum) and yam, benefiting from its savanna and transitional vegetation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which country hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup, the first held on African soil?
questions.explanation: South Africa hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup, the first World Cup held in Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who is credited with inventing the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which document is regarded as the supreme law of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is the supreme law of the land.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1986?
questions.explanation: Wole Soyinka became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1986.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a persistent, sustained fall in the general price level of goods and services in an economy?
questions.explanation: Deflation describes an ongoing, generalised decrease in prices across an economy, the opposite of inflation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which vitamin deficiency is most commonly associated with the disease scurvy?
questions.explanation: Scurvy is a disease resulting from a deficiency of Vitamin C, historically significant among sailors on long voyages without fresh fruit.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC)?
options: Organising and supervising elections in Nigeria
questions.explanation: INEC is Nigeria's independent body responsible for organising, conducting, and supervising elections at the federal and state levels.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for money a government spends exceeding its revenue, financed by borrowing?
questions.explanation: A budget deficit occurs when government spending exceeds its revenue in a given period.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Nigeria is a major member of which oil-exporting organisation?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is a member of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What term describes a country's shift from relying on oil towards other sectors of its economy?
questions.explanation: Economic diversification refers to reducing dependence on a single sector, like oil, by developing other sectors.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is Nigeria's main export commodity, alongside crude oil, in terms of historical economic importance?
questions.explanation: Cocoa has historically been one of Nigeria's most significant non-oil export commodities, particularly important before the discovery of oil.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is the largest producer of crude oil in Africa, based on long-established historical ranking?
questions.explanation: Nigeria has long been recognised as one of Africa's leading crude oil producers, historically ranking as the continent's largest producer for extended periods.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which African country was never formally colonised?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia successfully resisted European colonisation, notably defeating Italy at the Battle of Adwa in 1896.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for national statistics, including GDP figures?
questions.explanation: The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) compiles and publishes Nigeria's official statistics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, is located in which mountain range?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest is part of the Himalayan mountain range, on the border of Nepal and Tibet.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which regulatory body is responsible for accrediting academic programmes in Nigerian universities?
options: The Federal Ministry of Education alone, with no separate agency
The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB)
questions.explanation: The NUC is the regulatory body responsible for approving and accrediting academic programmes offered by Nigerian universities, ensuring they meet minimum quality standards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Nigeria won its first Olympic gold medal in which sport, in 1996?
questions.explanation: Chioma Ajunwa won Nigeria's first individual Olympic gold medal in the long jump at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which agency in Nigeria is primarily responsible for fighting financial and economic crimes?
questions.explanation: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) investigates financial crimes in Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which body regulates Nigeria's oil and gas sector, established after major reforms?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) is central to Nigeria's oil and gas industry.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the smallest country in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City, an independent city-state enclaved within Rome, Italy, is the smallest country in the world by land area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which is the largest continent by land area?
questions.explanation: Asia is the largest continent both by land area and population.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the name of Nigeria's National Assembly's upper chamber?
questions.explanation: The Senate is the upper chamber of Nigeria's bicameral National Assembly.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is Ghana's national football team commonly nicknamed?
questions.explanation: Ghana's senior men's national football team is popularly known as the Black Stars, distinct from Nigeria's Super Eagles and Cameroon's Indomitable Lions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary role of a Vice-Chancellor in a Nigerian university, such as UNILORIN?
options: Serving as the elected student union president
Serving as an external auditor of the university's accounts
Managing only the university's sports facilities
Serving as the chief executive and academic head of the university
questions.explanation: A Vice-Chancellor is the chief executive and principal academic officer of a Nigerian university, responsible for its overall administration and academic direction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Where is the headquarters of the African Union (AU) located?
questions.explanation: The African Union's headquarters is in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian author wrote the celebrated novel 'Things Fall Apart'?
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe wrote 'Things Fall Apart' (1958), one of the most widely read and celebrated African novels in modern literary history.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which international body is primarily responsible for setting global standards and rules for international trade?
questions.explanation: The WTO is the international organisation specifically responsible for establishing and enforcing global rules governing trade between nations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who was Nigeria's Head of State during the civil war (1967-1970)?
questions.explanation: General Yakubu Gowon led Nigeria as Head of State during the Nigerian Civil War.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian agency regulates telecommunications?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) regulates the telecommunications industry.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these is a key organ of the United Nations responsible for peace and security?
questions.explanation: The UN Security Council has primary responsibility for maintaining international peace and security.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a government budget in which planned expenditure exceeds planned revenue?
questions.explanation: A deficit budget occurs when a government's planned spending exceeds its expected revenue, often requiring borrowing to cover the shortfall.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the capital city of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Abuja became Nigeria's capital in 1991, replacing Lagos.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who became Nigeria's President following the 2023 general elections?
questions.explanation: Bola Ahmed Tinubu was declared winner of the 2023 presidential election and inaugurated President.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the chemical symbol for common table salt?
questions.explanation: Table salt is chemically sodium chloride, represented by the formula NaCl.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the practice of a country restricting imports through tariffs or quotas to protect domestic industries?
questions.explanation: Protectionism refers to government policies that restrict international trade, such as tariffs and quotas, to shield domestic industries from foreign competition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the minimum wage policy area primarily concerned with?
options: The lowest legal pay for workers
questions.explanation: Minimum wage laws set the lowest amount employers can legally pay workers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which African country has the largest population?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which country lies to the west of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Republic of Benin borders Nigeria to the west.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the total value of a country's exports minus its imports?
questions.explanation: Trade balance is the difference between the value of a country's exports and imports.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a major seaport in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Apapa Port in Lagos is one of Nigeria's busiest seaports.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which body regulates Nigeria's currency and monetary policy?
questions.explanation: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is responsible for monetary policy and currency issuance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these is a common symptom used to detect an ongoing pandemic caused by a novel virus?
questions.explanation: Fever is a common early symptom monitored during outbreaks of infectious respiratory illnesses.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which country lies to the east of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Cameroon borders Nigeria to the east.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which sport is Nigeria's Super Eagles primarily known for?
questions.explanation: The Super Eagles are Nigeria's national men's football team.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which state is known as the 'Centre of Excellence'?
questions.explanation: Lagos State is popularly nicknamed the 'Centre of Excellence'.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Nigeria contributes troops to peacekeeping missions mainly under which body?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is a major contributor of troops to UN peacekeeping operations across the world.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: In what year did Nigeria gain independence from Britain?
questions.explanation: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on October 1, 1960.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who was Nigeria's first executive President under the 1979 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Shehu Shagari became Nigeria's first executive President in 1979 under the Second Republic.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who is credited as the first President of the United States of America?
questions.explanation: George Washington served as the first President of the United States from 1789 to 1797.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian President served two terms consecutively from 2015 to 2023?
questions.explanation: Muhammadu Buhari served as President of Nigeria from 2015 to 2023.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which organisation is primarily concerned with global health issues?
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) coordinates international public health matters.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Nigeria is bordered by which of these countries to the north?
questions.explanation: Nigeria shares its northern border with the Niger Republic.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these is Nigeria's national football stadium located in Abuja?
questions.explanation: The Moshood Abiola National Stadium in Abuja is Nigeria's main national stadium.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: How many local government areas does Nigeria have?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is divided into 774 Local Government Areas.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF)?
options: Providing humanitarian and developmental assistance to children worldwide
questions.explanation: UNICEF is a United Nations agency specifically dedicated to providing humanitarian aid and support for children's health, education, and welfare worldwide.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which river is the longest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile River, flowing through northeastern Africa, is traditionally regarded as the world's longest river.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who was the first Secretary-General of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: Trygve Lie of Norway was the first UN Secretary-General, serving from 1946 to 1952.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who was Nigeria's President when it returned to civilian rule in 1999?
questions.explanation: Olusegun Obasanjo was sworn in as President in 1999, marking the start of the Fourth Republic.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian leader was assassinated in a coup in February 1976?
questions.explanation: General Murtala Mohammed was assassinated in an attempted coup on 13 February 1976.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following countries shares a land border with Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria shares land borders with Niger, Chad, Cameroon, and Benin Republic; Ghana, South Africa, and Kenya are not bordering countries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which is the smallest country in the world by land area?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is the smallest independent state in the world by both area and population.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian agency oversees standards for products and services?
questions.explanation: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) sets and enforces product and service standards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which international financial institution provides loans mainly for development projects?
questions.explanation: The World Bank provides financial and technical assistance for development projects globally.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which arm of government in Nigeria is primarily responsible for interpreting laws and administering justice?
questions.explanation: The Judiciary is the arm of government responsible for interpreting laws and adjudicating disputes, distinct from the law-making Legislature and law-enforcing Executive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The Nigerian Civil War is also known by what name?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Civil War (1967–1970) is also referred to as the Biafran War, after the breakaway Republic of Biafra.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for managing the environment and combating issues like erosion?
questions.explanation: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) enforces environmental regulations in Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What are the colours of the Nigerian flag?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian flag has three vertical stripes: green, white, and green.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which agency regulates food and drugs in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) regulates food, drugs, and related products.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which policy reform did the Nigerian government implement in 2023 regarding petrol prices?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian government removed the petrol subsidy in 2023, significantly raising pump prices.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these best describes inflation?
options: A fall in general price levels
A general and sustained rise in price levels
questions.explanation: Inflation refers to a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which city hosts the headquarters of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The United Nations headquarters is located in New York City, USA.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these is Nigeria's main export commodity?
questions.explanation: Crude oil is Nigeria's principal export and main source of foreign exchange.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who succeeded Umaru Musa Yar'Adua as President after his death in office?
questions.explanation: Goodluck Jonathan, then Vice President, succeeded Yar'Adua after his death in 2010.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these best defines 'literacy rate'?
options: The number of schools in a country
The number of years of compulsory education
The percentage of people who can read and write
questions.explanation: Literacy rate measures the proportion of a population able to read and write.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which sport is most associated with the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON)?
questions.explanation: AFCON is Africa's premier international men's football competition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian-born boxer became a world middleweight and light-heavyweight champion in the 1960s?
questions.explanation: Dick Tiger was a Nigerian boxer who held both the world middleweight and light-heavyweight titles in the 1960s.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who led the secession attempt that led to the Biafran War?
questions.explanation: Colonel Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu declared the Republic of Biafra in 1967.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary role of the executive arm of government?
questions.explanation: The executive arm, headed by a President or Governor, is primarily responsible for implementing and enforcing the laws made by the legislature.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these is Nigeria's longest river?
questions.explanation: The Niger River is the longest river in Nigeria and gives the country its name.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian musician is popularly known as one of the pioneers of Afrobeat music?
questions.explanation: Fela Anikulapo Kuti is widely regarded as the founder of Afrobeat music.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: The University of Ilorin (UNILORIN) is located in which state?
questions.explanation: UNILORIN, established in 1975, is located in Ilorin, the capital city of Kwara State.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the process of transferring government-owned enterprises to private ownership?
questions.explanation: Privatisation is the transfer of ownership of businesses from the government to private entities.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian became the first African and first woman Director-General of the World Trade Organization?
questions.explanation: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became the WTO's first female and first African Director-General in 2021.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for a system of government headed by a king or queen whose powers are limited by a constitution?
questions.explanation: A constitutional monarchy is a system in which a monarch serves as head of state, but their powers are limited and defined by a constitution, unlike an absolute monarchy.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who is regarded as the Father of Nigeria's Independence and its first Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa served as Nigeria's first and only Prime Minister from 1960 to 1966.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: How many geopolitical zones does Nigeria have?
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 6 geopolitical zones: North Central, North East, North West, South East, South South, and South West.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What does the abbreviation 'NAFDAC' stand for in the Nigerian context?
options: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control
National Association for Drug and Chemical Control
Nigerian Agency for Food and Drug Coordination
National Authority for Food, Drugs, and Cosmetics
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates and controls the manufacture, importation, and sale of food, drugs, and related products in Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which country is the largest by land area in the world?
questions.explanation: Russia is the largest country in the world by land area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Kwara State, where UNILORIN is situated, is often referred to by which nickname reflecting its position in Nigeria?
options: The Food Basket of the Nation
questions.explanation: Kwara State is popularly known as the 'State of Harmony', reflecting its historical position bridging Nigeria's north and south.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is Nigeria's national anthem's first line?
questions.explanation: 'Arise, O Compatriots' is the opening line of Nigeria's current national anthem.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: How many times had Nigeria won the Africa Cup of Nations as of the most recent editions before 2023?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's Super Eagles had won AFCON three times (1980, 1994, 2013) prior to the 2023/2024 edition.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What term describes long-term shifts in temperature and weather patterns largely due to human activity?
questions.explanation: Climate change refers to significant, long-term changes in global weather patterns.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What does AfCFTA stand for?
options: African Currency and Finance Trade Agreement
questions.explanation: AfCFTA aims to create a single market for goods and services across Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Nigeria's national female football team is nicknamed what?
questions.explanation: The Super Falcons are Nigeria's senior women's national football team.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the official currency of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The Naira is Nigeria's official currency, issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which regional force did Nigeria play a leading role in during peacekeeping in Liberia and Sierra Leone?
questions.explanation: ECOMOG (ECOWAS Monitoring Group) was a key peacekeeping force Nigeria led in West Africa.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary aim of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)?
options: Creating a single market for goods and services across African countries to boost intra-African trade
Restricting all trade between African nations
questions.explanation: AfCFTA aims to create a single continental market for goods and services, boosting intra-African trade by reducing tariffs and other trade barriers among member states.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following best describes the primary function of the Nigerian Police Force?
options: Maintaining law and order and enforcing criminal law
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Police Force is the primary law enforcement agency responsible for maintaining public order and enforcing criminal law across the country.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian city hosted the 2000/2003 All Africa Games?
questions.explanation: Abuja hosted the All Africa Games (COJA) in 2003.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these is NOT one of Nigeria's arms of government?
questions.explanation: Nigeria's three arms of government are the Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which global health body declared COVID-19 a pandemic in March 2020?
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a global pandemic in March 2020.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is a key function of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) relating to currency?
options: Issuing and regulating the country's currency (the Naira)
Setting the retail price of consumer goods
questions.explanation: One of the CBN's core functions is the sole authority to issue and regulate Nigeria's legal tender currency, the Naira.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon in July 1969.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the Nigerian legislative chamber that represents individual constituencies at the federal level, alongside the Senate?
questions.explanation: The House of Representatives, together with the Senate, forms Nigeria's bicameral National Assembly, with members representing federal constituencies.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian agency collects tax revenue for the federal government?
questions.explanation: The Federal Inland Revenue Service (FIRS) is responsible for assessing and collecting federal taxes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: How many states does Nigeria currently have?
questions.explanation: Nigeria has 36 states plus the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a communicable disease?
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is a communicable (infectious) disease caused by bacteria, unlike diabetes, hypertension, and cancer, which are non-communicable conditions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which of these gases is most associated with climate change and global warming?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas contributing to global warming.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the full meaning of IMF?
questions.explanation: The IMF works to ensure global monetary cooperation and financial stability.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the name of Nigeria's stock exchange?
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX) is Nigeria's main stock exchange.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which global sporting event features the Olympic Games and takes place every four years?
questions.explanation: The Olympic Games is a major international multi-sport event held every four years.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the term for the legal document that formally establishes the rules and structure of governance for a country?
questions.explanation: A constitution is the fundamental legal document that establishes the framework, powers, and limits of a country's system of governance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: What is the largest lake in Africa?
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria, bordered by Uganda, Kenya, and Tanzania, is the largest lake in Africa by surface area.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Nigeria returned to civilian rule (Fourth Republic) in what year?
questions.explanation: Nigeria transitioned back to democratic civilian rule in 1999, ending years of military governance.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which Nigerian author wrote the acclaimed novel 'Things Fall Apart'?
questions.explanation: Chinua Achebe wrote 'Things Fall Apart', one of the most widely read African novels.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Who designed the Nigerian flag?
questions.explanation: Michael Taiwo Akinkunmi designed Nigeria's national flag, adopted in 1960.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which renewable energy source relies on sunlight?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is generated by converting sunlight into electricity or heat.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which desert is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert in North Africa is the largest hot desert in the world.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which scientist developed the theory of relativity?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein developed the theory of relativity, revolutionising physics.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.text: Which body is responsible for organising elections in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: INEC (Independent National Electoral Commission) conducts and supervises elections in Nigeria.
